newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Tri Star to raise exports to M&S.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Tri Star to raise exports to M&S.

text.p: Marks & Spencer Plc is increasing imports from Sri Lanka by 40 to 50 percent over the next three years, a senior official of the local Tri Star Apparel Exports (Pte) Ltd said on Tuesday.
"Marks & Spencer has already taken steps to raise its current monthly intake of 800,000 to one million pieces by 40 to 50 percent," said the official, who declined to be named.
Tri Star is an associate of SR Gent Plc, a major supplier of Marks & Spencer, and has sold garments to the British department store for the past eight years.
The official said the U.S.-based Kikomo Group had also agreed to increase imports from Tri Star.
"Kikomo is raising imports to 600,000 pieces a month from the current 250,000," he said.
Israel's Gamma Club last month signed an agreement to raise purchases from Tri Star to $32 million from $5 million a year.
Tri Star is Sri Lanka's biggest garment manufacturer and exporter with 32 factories employing 28,000 workers.
Customs statistics in 1995 showed Tri Star to be the island's top corporate foreign exchange earner with 3.2 billion rupees ($55.17 million).
Sri Lanka's garments exports in 1995 were worth 94.9 billion rupees. The final 1996 figure was not immediately available but trade sources say it was expected to be higher than in the previous year.
